content.text:
Analysis complete. Section 6.1 does restrict us (the Company), so I assessed it against the fallback:

- **Term only, no tail**: bound "during the term of this Agreement" only — no post-term restriction (contrast §6.3, which binds HDI for the term *plus* two years, in our favour). The term is one year, auto-renewing, terminable on 90 days' notice (§4.1), so the effective restraint is short.
- **Bounded scope**: limited to "any project similar to the Site on the Internet" — an online-channel restriction only. Our catalog and offline business, and every other line of business, are untouched. This is not "any competing business."
- **Named products/competitors**: keyed to the defined term "Deerskin Products" (§1.1) and expressly named competitors (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled).
- **Carve-outs**: §6.2 preserves our right to run a closeout web site, and the "Deerskin Products" definition carves out closeout merchandise and the Joan Cook Catalog.

The only preferred-position element absent is an express internal-development/acquisition carve-out, which is a minor sub-element (and of limited relevance to a retail-channel restraint). This sits at the fallback and should not be redlined.

input.quote: Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled)
input.rationale: Section 6.1 is a restriction binding us (the Company), so it is in scope for this rule, but it sits at the playbook fallback and is therefore not redlined. It applies "during the term of this Agreement" only, with no post-term tail (by contrast §6.3 binds HDI for the term plus two years, which is in our favour), and the term is a single year, auto-renewing and terminable by either party on 90 days' notice (§4.1) — well inside the 12-month cap. Scope is bounded rather than open-ended: it reaches only "any project similar to the Site on the Internet," i.e. a single online channel, and only as to the defined "Deerskin Products" (§1.1) plus expressly named competitors (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled). Our catalog business, offline sales and all other lines of business are unaffected, so this is not the "any competing business" undefined scope that would be walk-away territory. Carve-outs also exist: §6.2 preserves our right to run a closeout web site, and the "Deerskin Products" definition excludes closeout merchandise and the Joan Cook Catalog. The only preferred-position element missing is an express internal-development/acquisition carve-out, which is a minor sub-element noted here rather than flagged, particularly as the restraint is a retail-channel exclusivity exchanged for HDI bearing all design, development and hosting costs (§1.2, §1.3).
